content.comment_body: Hello everyone. I'm facing a problem: I need to establish communication between a [version_no] PLC and a [product_name] using [product_name] V13 Basic, but I'm unsure about the process. Could someone provide guidance on this? Thanks.
On this [company_name] website, you can find an example for [version_no] in [product_name] Basic V11. [version_no] communication [url] Perhaps this resource can help you further.

Hello, I have a similar issue. I downloaded the example, have [product_name] V13 Basic, a [product_name] V8, and a [article_no] CPU. After following the sample and tutorial, I couldn't establish communication. Maybe the [product_name] version affects this. Could someone assist, please?

Hello [user_name], That tutorial explains how to connect a [product_name] with [version_no] using firmware V3. If you are using [version_no] with firmware V4.0, you need to enable GET/PUT communication in the hardware settings of your controller in [product_name] V13. This allows your PLC to operate as a server. Please refer to the attached screenshot.

In [product_name], you can create variables and set up a connection with [product_name]. Ensure you set the correct IP address for the [product_name]. Use the help section to search for VM Mapping to find addresses for inputs, outputs, and markers. For other signals, create virtual addresses (VM Mode) in the [product_name]. Note that the virtual addresses for [product_name] [article_no] differ from [article_no].

Thanks to everyone. Following your suggestions, running the program online, [product_name] reports communication problems with [product_name], but [product_name] V8 has correctly mapped the VM addresses. I'm wondering if it could be a network cable or switch issue. Right now, I'm testing a simple program that activates PLC input and output that controls the [product_name].

You can set up a small network using a switch by connecting your PC, PLC, and [product_name]. Ensure that all IP addresses are unique but within the same range, such as 192.168.0.x, and that subnet masks are the same (e.g., 255.255.255.0). If your PC can communicate with both the [product_name] and PLC simultaneously, and the IP settings are correct, everything should work.
Alright, I'll retry and check for potential mistakes based on your advice.
Here is the screen that appears when I try to connect online; you can see one of the connections shows an error. Perhaps this is causing the issue.
Hi, could you please attach your programs so I can help you?

Apologies for the delayed response. I experienced the same error but managed to resolve it, so I'm sharing this solution to help others. The tutorial mentions that you need to uncheck the 'Establish active connection' option; however, in [product_name] V13, this option is disabled in the window shown. You must locate and uncheck it elsewhere for everything to work. I have attached an image showing the option unchecked. Sorry, my [product_name] version is in Spanish.
